
### interdomain routing  {.smaller}


* so far: routing within one organization
* lots of trust/sharing: 
<hr class="vspace" />
* okay to send packets through (essentially) every router
* okay for any router to ‘announce’ any address
* okay to share (almost) full map of network 
<hr class="vspace" />
* not what we want for interdomain routing

### some business considerations 

![](/routing-bgp/texfig/some-business-considerations.figure-1.svg){fig-alt="network connection diagramannotated with who is paying: webhost pays to connect to ISP B and connects to ISPs A and C without payment; office pays to connect to ISPs B and C; school pays to connect to ISP D. ISP A connects to ISP C without payment; ISP B conects to ISP C without payment; ISP D pays to connect to ISP C."}

### some business considerations (exercise 1)

![](/routing-bgp/texfig/some-business-considerations.figure-2.svg){fig-alt="Route from webhost to ISP C to ISP D to office. The webhost does not pay for its connection to ISP C (but does for ISP B, which has an unpaid connection to ISP C). The office does pay for its connections to ISP B and D (and has no other connections)."}

::: {.myoverbox .vlow}

exercise: does this route make sense?

:::


### some business considerations (exercise 2)

![](/routing-bgp/texfig/some-business-considerations.figure-3.svg){fig-alt="Route from webhost to ISP B to office.
